name: lisp-cli
title: Common Lisp CLI
blurb: Common Lisp CLI on SBCL: byte-exact counting core, hand-rolled argv parser, dependency-free test harness, I/O through a structure of functions

verify.name: usage-error
verify.cmd: set +e; ./bin/{{ npm_name }} --bogus > /dev/null 2>&1; status=$?; echo "exit status: $status"; test "$status" -eq 2

verify.name: missing-file
verify.cmd: set +e; ./bin/{{ npm_name }} nope.txt > /dev/null 2>&1; status=$?; echo "exit status: $status"; test "$status" -eq 1

verify.name: parity
verify.cmd:
mkdir -p .parity && printf 'alpha beta
gamma delta
' > .parity/p1.txt && printf 'alpha beta
gamma delta' > .parity/p2.txt && printf 'h\303\251llo w\303\266rld
' > .parity/p3.txt && : > .parity/p4.txt && printf 'a	b\vc d
' > .parity/p5.txt && for f in .parity/p*.txt; do ours=$(./bin/{{ npm_name }} "$f" | awk '{print $1, $2, $3}'); theirs=$(wc -l -w -c < "$f" | awk '{print $1, $2, $3}'); test "$ours" = "$theirs" || { echo "mismatch on $f: $ours vs $theirs"; exit 1; }; done && echo 'every fixture matches wc'
